name: International
scope: The internationalization of UAP disclosure itself — the degree to which the subject moves from a purely national matter toward coordinated action between states. Foreign national acts count only as data points proving a rung of internationalization.
excludes: The domestic depth of any foreign government's UAP program (those tracks are US-scoped). A foreign act is credited here for internationalization, not re-measured for domestic maturity.
method: First-principles ladder ordered by cross-border commitment, formality, cost and irreversibility. Non-ontological: rungs measure inter-state acts, not the nature of the phenomenon.
read: The non-linearity is the story: the universal body — the UN — is a dead letter, while bilateral and Five Eyes cooperation quietly advance. Disclosure internationalizes through intelligence alliances, not open institutions. The top rung is capped by design.
summary: The international dimension has climbed from isolated national programs to broad parallel recognition — France and the USSR ran structured state programs by the late 1970s, and engagement now spans the UK, Japan, Chile and Argentina. The operational frontier sits at bilateral contact and a nascent, US-led Five Eyes caucus. The top rung — a binding, transparent global regime — is structurally capped by national-security sensitivity.
sourcingQuality: Strong at rungs 1-2 and 5 (official agency pages, Russian Academy of Sciences journal, AARO FOIA). Rung 4 mixes primary and official-proceeding (Japan) evidence.

rungs.title: Individual state initiative
rungs.oneLiner: A non-US state formally engages. e.g. France GEIPAN 1977; USSR Setka 1978.
rungs.firstPrinciples: First act above baseline — a state other than the US formally engages (program, hearing, official body), proving the subject escaped its national container.
rungs.statusRationale: France (1977) and the USSR (1978) ran structured state programs near-simultaneously — the subject was escaping national borders in both East and West at once.

sources.label: USSR — 'Setka' state program 1978-1990, documented by Platov & Sokolov, Herald of the Russian Academy of Sciences (2000)

rungs.title: Parallel recognition
rungs.oneLiner: Multiple states engage independently. e.g. UK, France, USSR, Japan, Chile, Argentina.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Multiple states engage independently, proving a pattern across political systems, not one state's curiosity.
rungs.statusRationale: Independent engagement is proven across Europe, the Soviet sphere, East Asia and South America — under radically different systems.

sources.label: Chile — CEFAA/SEFAA, created 3 Oct 1997 by DGAC
Japan — MoD reporting/analysis directive (2020), repeated Diet scrutiny (2024), cross-party UAP caucus (June 2024)
sources.note: Kantei pages video-only; caucus documentation proceeding-level

rungs.title: Intergovernmental recognition
rungs.oneLiner: UN Decision 33/426 (1978) produced no body, no follow-through in 48 years.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A multilateral body (UN/NATO/regional) substantively engages, making the subject an international matter, not just a collection of national ones.
rungs.statusRationale: The only instance — UN GA Decision 33/426 (1978) — was adopted but created no agency, and 48 years of silence followed. A reversible gesture with zero function and zero successor is Not yet, not Partial: nothing operational was ever started.

sources.label: No qualifying source for substantive engagement (UN records confirm the 1978 decision produced no body)

rungs.title: Bilateral cooperation
rungs.oneLiner: Cross-border contact exists. e.g. GEIPAN-CEFAA 2014, Japan-US. Partial: no UAP-specific accord.
rungs.firstPrinciples: Two states move from independent domestic action to actual cross-border interaction — the first operational rung.
rungs.statusRationale: Official contact and coordination are demonstrated (GEIPAN-CEFAA 2014; Japan-US 2020/2023; AARO's ongoing international engagement), but no public UAP-specific agreement, joint intake standard or recurring case-sharing pipeline exists. The 1971 US-USSR agreement is a tangential precedent (nuclear risk reduction), not UAP cooperation.

sources.label: AARO FY2025 report — ongoing international engagement/information exchange
Japan MoD statement of close US coordination on unidentified objects (Diet, Nov 2023)
1971 US-USSR Agreement on Measures to Reduce the Risk of Outbreak of Nuclear War, Art. 3 (unidentified objects on missile-warning systems) — Avalon Project, Yale Law
sources.note: tangential precedent — nuclear risk reduction, not UAP-specific cooperation

rungs.title: Multilateral coordination
rungs.oneLiner: AARO Five Eyes UAP Caucus, May 2023 (FOIA). Partial: US-led, nascent, no shared standards.
rungs.firstPrinciples: More than two states coordinate through a standing mechanism with shared standards/data/protocols.
rungs.statusRationale: The AARO Five Eyes UAP Caucus (inaugural 24 May 2023) is a real multilateral forum, but US-led, inside an existing SIGINT alliance, with shared-database items only aspirational, and one member (UK) publicly disclaims current UAP investigation. Highly reversible, no treaty basis.

sources.label: AARO Five Eyes UAP Caucus — FOIA-released agenda + NASA FACA meeting confirmation (May 2023)

rungs.title: Comprehensive international framework
rungs.oneLiner: No binding regime. Structurally capped by sensitive sources, methods, locations.
rungs.firstPrinciples: A binding, transparent international regime governs the subject — shared standards, open reporting, common protocols, institutional permanence.
rungs.statusRationale: No treaty, no UN agency, no binding data-sharing regime. Structurally capped: full international data-sharing would require sharing sensitive sensor sources, methods and locations — unprecedented even among allies. Any future framework would be partial-by-design. Inaccessibility is a feature of the subject's sensitivity, not a maturity failure.

excludedClaims.reason: A single-member-organized hearing; Congress took no position; the 'bodies' were discredited. A weak secondary data point, never official recognition.
No agency was ever established (see rung 3).
Nuclear arms control with incidental relevance to unidentified objects on warning systems.

excludedClaims.claim: George Knapp's Soviet files — dramatic claims (Unit 73790, reverse-engineering, downed MiGs)
excludedClaims.reason: The congressional testimony is a genuine primary record and program existence (Setka) is established, but the extraordinary operational/technological claims are journalist-mediated documents with public authentication still incomplete. Excluded as bilateral cooperation (document transfer, not state-to-state cooperation). The written testimony (House Oversight, 9 Sept 2025) is entered into the record — the filing is verifiable; the extraordinary claims within it are not corroborated.

crossTrackNotes: Non-linearity is a finding, not a flaw: rung 3 (UN) is Not yet while rungs 4-5 are Partial, because cooperation flows through intelligence alliances while universal bodies stay a dead letter. A foreign state's internal act proves an internationalization rung; it does not re-measure that country's domestic maturity.
